statement: A catalogue row marked 'confirmed' resolves to an encoded entry with the same id.
rationale: The catalogue is the index and the entries are the records. If they disagree about what a thing is called, every join across them is unreliable and 'confirmed' status means nothing.
prediction: Every catalogue row with status 'confirmed' resolves to an encoded entry sharing its id. Entries indexed by no registry are reported but do not falsify.

revisions.was: A keystone has exactly one identity: the id in data/shadow_catalogue.json and the id of its encoded entry are the same string — checked in both directions.
revisions.became: Only the confirmed-row-implies-entry direction falsifies; entries absent from every registry are reported.
revisions.because: Merging main added 31 entries and a second registry, data/candidates.json, whose 12 rows overlap the catalogue in zero ids. The reverse direction was a fair requirement while the catalogue was the only index; enforcing it now would settle by fiat which of two registries is canonical. That decision is open as U-H001-2 and belongs to whoever makes it explicitly.

last_result.summary: all 9 confirmed catalogue ids resolve to encoded entries; 24 entries indexed nowhere
